key_insight: RoboWits introduces a bi-manual robotic benchmark that exposes gaps in current systems by systematically testing cognitive reasoning, creative tool use, and robustness under unexpected conditions, revealing that skill-level performance alone doesn't capture real-world problem-solving ability.
problem_solved: Current robotic benchmarks focus on low-level skill execution and fail to evaluate higher-level cognitive reasoning and adaptability needed when robots encounter unexpected challenges or must repurpose objects as tools.
method: Design a suite of bi-manual tasks that require creative tool use and problem solving under unexpected perturbations and environmental changes.
Build a scalable benchmark pipeline (simulation + real-world proxies) enabling systematic generation of diverse challenge scenarios and controlled evaluation of robustness and creativity.
Define task-level metrics capturing success, adaptability, tool-use creativity, and failure modes to compare robot policies and human baselines.
impact: RoboWits provides practitioners a targeted benchmark to develop and evaluate systems that go beyond dexterity—encouraging research on reasoning, affordance discovery, and resilient behavior in real-world robotic agents. Adoption can accelerate progress toward robots that safely handle novel, unstructured situations.
visual_elements: Overview diagram: pipeline from task generation → simulated/real trials → metrics and analysis
Task gallery: side-by-side images showing standard vs. unexpected challenge variants and creative tool-use solutions
Radar/metric chart: axes for success rate, adaptability, creativity score, and robustness to visualize comparative performance
Failure mode icons: small panels depicting common failure types (e.g., mis-usage of objects, brittle policies, perceptual errors)
paper_title: RoboWits: Unexpected Challenges for Robotic Creative Problem Solving
paper_authors: Chunru Lin, Hongxin Zhang, Fenghao Yu, Zhehuan Chen, Thomas L. Griffiths
